extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic geometry and number theory (readers of Mochizuki's IUT papers)
extracted.subtask_description: Formal construction and analysis of the multiradial representation and log-theta-lattice in the context of Inter-Universal Teichmüller Theory III, including log-links, log-shells, Kummer isomorphisms, and log-volume estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ind1 (D‑prime‑strip automorphism indeterminacy)
rubrics_metrics.description: the indeterminacies induced by the automorphisms of the procession of D(cid:3)-prime-strips Prc(n,◦D(cid:3)T) that gives rise to the tensor packets of (a)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiradial representation data n,◦RLGP are regarded up to these Ind1 indeterminacies; they arise from automorphisms of the procession of D‑prime‑strips and are handled by working functorially with processions (see Theorem 3.11(i)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ind2 (F(cid:3)×μ‑prime‑strip/Z× indeterminacy)
rubrics_metrics.description: the [“non-(Ind1) portion” of the] indeterminacies that arise from the automorphisms of the F(cid:3)×μ-prime-strips that appear in the Θ×μ LGP-link, i.e., in particular, at [for simplicity] v ∈ Vnon, the (cid:6)Z×-indeterminacies acting on local copies of 'O×μ'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These indeterminacies act on copies of O×μ and figure in the definition of the multiradial representation; compatibility statements and constructions (e.g., cyclotomic rigidity) are formulated modulo Ind2 (cf. Theorem 3.11(i),(iii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ind3 (upper semi-compatibility indeterminacy of Kummer isomorphisms)
rubrics_metrics.description: as one varies m ∈ Z, the Kummer isomorphisms of tensor packets of log-shells are 'upper semi-compatible' relative to the log-links of the n-th column of the LGP-Gaussian log-theta-lattice, involving certain natural inclusions '⊆' at vQ ∈ Vnon and certain natural surjections at vQ ∈ Varc
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This indeterminacy reflects 'upper semi-compatibility' (not full compatibility) and leads to 'substantial distortion' in constructions that depend on local additive integral structures (cf. Proposition 3.5, Theorem 3.11(ii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiradial Representation composition and constructibility
rubrics_metrics.description: n,◦RLGP is the collection of data consisting of (a) tensor packets of log-shells; (b) splitting monoids of LGP-monoids acting on the tensor packets of (a); (c) copies, labeled by j ∈ F(cid:3)l, of the multiplicative monoid of nonzero elements of the number field Fmod acting on the tensor packets of (a), regarded up to indeterminacies Ind1 and Ind2
rubrics_metrics.guidance: n,◦RLGP may be constructed via an algorithm in the procession of D‑prime‑strips Prc(n,◦D(cid:3)T), functorial with respect to isomorphisms; permutation symmetries and bi-coricity induce compatible poly‑isomorphisms between such multiradial representations (see Theorem 3.11(i) and Theorem A(i)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Log‑Kummer Correspondence (existence and compatibility of inverse Kummer isomorphisms)
rubrics_metrics.description: the inverses of the Kummer isomorphisms associated to various F‑prime‑strips and NF‑bridges induce 'inverse Kummer' isomorphisms between the vertically coric data (a),(b),(c) of the multiradial representation and the corresponding Frobenioid‑theoretic data arising from each Θ±ellNF‑Hodge theater
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As m varies, the corresponding Kummer isomorphisms of splitting monoids and labelled copies of Fmod are mutually compatible relative to the log‑links in the sense that any relations via log‑links consist only of roots of unity; tensor packet Kummer isomorphisms are subject to Ind3. These compatibilities are tied to log-volume calculations (see Theorem 3.11(ii), Proposition 3.5, Proposition 3.10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Θ×μ LGP‑Link compatibility of Kummer isomorphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: the various Kummer isomorphisms satisfy compatibility properties with the horizontal Θ LGP‑links: tensor packets of log-shells are compatible with the unit group portion '(−)(cid:3)×μ' of the Θ LGP‑link; identity automorphisms on splitting monoids and labelled copies of Fmod are compatible with the Θ LGP‑link (modulo Ind2 and via cyclotomic rigidity)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compatibility statements are precise in Theorem 3.11(iii): they link the Kummer isomorphisms to the unit/value group decompositions and rely on cyclotomic rigidity constructions from IUTchI and IUTchII.

rubrics_metrics.name: Log‑volume inequality (Theorem B)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define −|log(Θ)| as the procession‑normalized mono‑analytic log‑volume of the holomorphic hull of the union of possible images of a Θ‑pilot object (subject to Ind1, Ind2, Ind3), and −|log(q)| as the procession‑normalized mono‑analytic log‑volume of the image of a q‑pilot object (not regarded as subject to Ind1–3). Then −|log(Θ)| ∈ R and −|log(Θ)| ≥ −|log(q)|.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalently, for any real CΘ with −|log(Θ)| ≤ CΘ·|log(q)| one has CΘ ≥ −1. |log(q)|>0 is computable from q‑parameters of the elliptic curve at v∈Vbad; the result underpins the 'negativity' (hyperbolicity) statement in this IUT context (see Theorem B and Corollary 3.12).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑interference / mutual compatibility property
rubrics_metrics.description: the multiplicative monoids constituted by the splitting monoids of LGP‑monoids and copies of F×mod 'do not interfere', relative to arrows in the log‑Kummer correspondence, with the local units at v ∈ V that give rise to the log‑shells
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For splitting monoids this follows from canonical splittings (up to roots of unity) of theta/Gaussian monoids (constant multiple rigidity); for copies of F×mod it follows from the algebraic‑number‑theory fact that an element integral at every valuation is a root of unity. These compatibility properties are detailed in Theorem 3.11(ii) and Theorem A(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cyclotomic rigidity immunity to Z× indeterminacies
rubrics_metrics.description: the cyclotomic rigidity isomorphisms appearing in the Kummer theory around splitting monoids and copies of F×mod are immune to the (cid:6)Z×‑indeterminacies that act on copies of O×μ arising in F×μ‑prime‑strips appearing in the Θ×μ LGP‑link
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This property ensures compatibility of cyclotomic rigidity isomorphisms with horizontal Θ LGP‑links and is part of the detailed compatibility statements in Theorem 3.11(iii); references include constructions from IUTchI Example 5.1(v).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between F_MOD and F_mod constructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Two natural constructions of the global Frobenioid associated to Fmod: ((MOD) Rational Function Torsor Version) depends only on the multiplicative structure of F×mod; ((mod) Local Fractional Ideal Version) involves additive local module structures of localizations Kv and thus is subject to 'upper semi‑compatibility' indeterminacy (Ind3)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the multiradial viewpoint, F_MOD is 'biased toward multiplicative structures' and rigid but less suited to explicit computation, while F_mod is 'biased toward additive structures' and suited to explicit estimates (cf. Fig. I.7, Remarks 3.6.2, 3.10.1, and Corollary 3.12).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and construction of log‑link, pre‑log‑shell, and log‑shell
rubrics_metrics.description: The tautological log‑link †F log→ log(†F) relates a given F‑prime‑strip †F to a collection of ind‑topological modules Ψ∼†Fv (the 'log(†Fv)') constructed via perfection and (p_v‑adic or complex) logarithms; the image in Ψ∼ of the submonoid of Gv(†Πv)‑invariants of Ψ× is called the pre‑log‑shell, and after a normalization factor one obtains the log‑shell I†Fv
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructions differ for v∈Vnon (p‑adic/perfection, PV‑adic logarithm) and v∈Varc (complex/logarithmic covering); log‑shells are algorithmically constructible from the given prime‑strip data and are regarded as objects associated to codomains of log‑links (cf. Definition 1.1 and AbsTopIII references).

rubrics_metrics.name: Algorithmic constructibility and functoriality of constructions
rubrics_metrics.description: the natural, algorithmically constructible assignments (e.g., Ψcns(†F), tautological log‑links, topological field structures on Ψ∼, and the multiradial representation n,◦RLGP) are functorial with respect to isomorphisms of the underlying processions/prime‑strips
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This algorithmic, functorial nature is emphasized (e.g., via IUTchII Corollary 4.6 and Theorem 3.11(i)); it is crucial for defining permutation symmetries and poly‑isomorphisms between processions and for making log‑volume computations canonical up to the stated indeterminacies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kummer‑detachment (passage Frobenius‑like → étale‑like)
rubrics_metrics.description: the operation of Kummer‑detachment passes from Frobenius‑like versions of objects to étale‑like versions in order to obtain vertically coric versions and then multiradial objects; this operation is possible precisely because of compatibility of the multiradial representation with the Θ LGP‑link and the indeterminacies (Ind1, Ind2, Ind3)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kummer‑detachment is a core procedural step in relating arithmetic holomorphic structures at different vertical lines and is used in the log‑volume proofs (see Fig. I.8 and the proof sketch of Corollary 3.12).

rubrics_metrics.name: Log‑volumes as intrinsic invariants and negativity/hyperbolicity analogy
rubrics_metrics.description: the log‑volume of the holomorphic hull of the union of possible images of the Θ‑pilot object (subject to indeterminacies) tautologically computes intrinsic properties of the q‑pilot object, leading to a negativity statement for |log(Θ)| analogous to metric hyperbolicity (e.g., Gauss‑Bonnet or Hasse invariant inequalities)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The argument shows two tautologically equivalent ways to compute q‑pilot log‑volume (Fig. I.8) and yields the inequality −|log(Θ)| ≥ −|log(q)|; the discussion draws explicit analogies to classical complex and p‑adic Teichmüller theory (see Remarks 3.12.1–3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of q‑pilot and Θ‑pilot objects and their log‑volumes
rubrics_metrics.description: a q‑pilot object is the arithmetic divisor determined by the zero locus of the elements 'q' at v∈Vbad and has procession‑normalized mono‑analytic log‑volume −|log(q)|>0; a Θ‑pilot object arises from the zero locus of a collection of theta values and its holomorphic hull log‑volume −|log(Θ)| may a priori be +∞ but is treated as a procession‑normalized mono‑analytic log‑volume
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notation −|log(Θ)| is used to express that −|log(Θ)| should be regarded as a positive real multiple of −|log(q)| plus a possible error term (potentially +∞); careful normalization (averaging over labels j ∈ F(cid:3)l) is used in statements (see Definition 3.8 and Corollary 3.12).
